newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares score 15th record close of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares score 15th record close of 1997.

text.p: Norwegian shares, taking a cue from Wall Street, powered to an all-time high in heavy trade on Thursday but the market outlook was uncertain, dealers said.

Oslo's Total share index closed 0.42 percent higher for a record close of 1,060.78 points. Turnover was 1.2 billion crowns. The shipping, industry and insurance indexes all rose, but the banking index was down slightly.
"We followed Wall Street, and interest rates fell somewhat at home," one dealer said. "But the market looks uncertain in the United States, and it reflects on Norway."
The stock exchange hit an intra-trading high of 1,062.81 in the first hour of trading. It then lost ground before taking off again in the last hour of the session after Wall Street opened higher.

Analysts say a mild correction might be expected soon at the bourse, which has scored 15 record closes in January in a liquidity-driven bull run. But they also say it all depends on U.S. developments.
Among the winners on Thursday was Saga Petroleum, whose A share rose 1.22 percent to 124 crowns.
